newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TEJ RISES ON INVESTOR INTEREST,AWAITED DEAL.
newsitem.headline: TEJ RISES ON INVESTOR INTEREST,AWAITED DEAL.

text.p: Clothing company Towles, Edgar Jacobs Ltd (TEJ) shares jumped on Monday ahead of an expected announcement on further acqusitions, dealers said.

The tightly-held share jumped 15.11 percent, or 210 cents, to 16 rand, bringing its gains to over 430 percent since Western Cape-based investment group CapeStar Growth Investments bought a 44 percent stake in TEJ on June 23.

"It's the flavour of the month stock and has top brass management. They look at investments of not less than two million rand and pump in cash and recapitalise them with a potential listing down the line," a dealer said.
CapeStar plans to restructure TEJ into an investment holding company, before listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's investment trusts sector.
The company will hold a rights issue as part of its plans to make between four and six investments over the next 12 months.
Dealers said the first of these investments was likely to be announced in mid-August.
CapeStar plans to target investments of a minimum of two million rand in projects in tourism, agribusiness, the expansion of export-led manufacturing, local media and property and financial services.

CapeStar consists of a consortium of investors led by former Massmart director Michael Rubin, Capital Partners and Fedsure Asset Management which paid eight million rand for 44 percent of TEJ's issued ordinary share capital, including 1.1 million previously held by the Jacobs family.
